text:
Mia: Heads up — finance flagged a mismatch between our committed throughput model and billing report for ACME's Dedicated pool.
Sanjay: How big is the discrepancy?
Mia: They signed 100k reqs/min sustained but billing shows reserved usage counted as ~80k/min. Could be mapping to vGPU types or packing.
Linda: Are we sure it's not metric windowing? Finance uses a 5-min aggregation, our model sims use 1-min spikes.
Rahul: Quick back-of-envelope: if avg per-GPU sustained = 2.5k reqs/min, 100k -> 40 GPUs. Billing shows capacity equivalent to ~32 GPUs. That explains the ~80k number.
Olivia: Any chance autoscaling bursts were mis-attributed to "burst" capacity rather than reserved?
billing-bot: Invoice #ACM-987: Reserved capacity utilization: 80% — see billing console https://billing.redwood/ACM-987 (generated 2051234500)
Sanjay: Looks like our routing policy marks some traffic as "burst" when queue latency < 20ms. Those don't decrement the committed counter.
Mia: Action items: infra verify node packing + routing attribution; finance confirm billing calc and aggregation window; acct exec prep customer note if we owe credits.
Linda: Also note region constraint — this pool is in eu-west-2 where we recently moved to A100v5-equivalent hosts. If the customer's model ran on an older kernel variant we may have fallen back to a different instance SKU that the billing mapper treats differently.
Olivia: I can repro in staging by replaying their 1-min steady load. Will run a job this afternoon and post logs.
Rahul: Paste of my quick numbers for visibility:
```
requested_throughput = 100_000 req/min
avg_gpu_throughput = 2500 req/min  # conservative
# GPUs required = ceil(requested_throughput / avg_gpu_throughput)
= 40 GPUs
# Billing equivalent observed = 80% -> ~32 GPUs
# Gap = 8 GPUs -> possible rounding/sku mismatch/aggregation window
```
Olivia: Test kicked off: job id staging-load-20512. Will include per-node req/min and kernel version.
Sanjay: Filed INF ticket INF-4532 and linked to billing: https://redwood.atlassian/INF-4532 — assigning to @Mia and @Linda.
billing-bot: Note: adjusting invoices requires Finance Ops approval. @Linda please triage.
Mia: If tests confirm, ops should prepare a retroactive credit calc: gap_gpus * hours * unit_cost. Finance to confirm policy.
Linda: Acknowledged. I'll pull the invoice timeline and check aggregation windows.
Rahul: Long-term fix ideas: (1) unify committed-metering to node-level rather than vGPU slices, (2) avoid counting fallback SKUs as reserved if they satisfy SLA, (3) surface a "metering preview" for customers.
Olivia: Posting initial staging results shortly. If we can narrow to packing mismatch we can hotfix routing policy quickly.
Mia: Sync in 30 mins after Olivia posts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
